standings.method: Every club on the official page was transcribed this session and compared field by field with data/standings.csv (the repository's own transcription) and data/model/snapshot.json (the model's input table).

results.feed_coverage_note: 13 of the 14 Week-10 games had no final score in the committed feed before this session; the LAC @ BAL Monday game had not been played when the pages were read.

sign_convention.conclusion: Positive correlation proves the mirrored closing line is expressed as points the HOME team is expected to win by (positive = home favourite).

blend_test.fit: margin ~ 1 + market_line + model_line on 2025, tested on 2026
blend_test.interpretation: A model weight at or below zero means the model's disagreement with the market was wrong on average in the test window; a positive weight with a lower test MAE means genuine incremental information.

method.ratings: Two-way ridge fixed effect on non-garbage-time plays: EPA ~ offense team + defense team + home. Prior season weighted 0.4.
method.note: Ratings for week W use only weeks < W of the current season plus the previous season at 40% weight, so the backtest has no look-ahead.

lines.market_provenance: The market column is a consensus closing line carried in the mirrored feed (nflverse). It is not a book price, and the repository holds no opening number and no moneyline price.

method.depth_charts: Official club depth charts, https://www.<club>/team/depth-chart, transcribed 2026-11-12. nfl.com publishes no depth chart: https://www.nfl.com/teams/kansas-city-chiefs/depth-chart returns 404 (re-checked 2026-11-13).
method.injuries: Official nfl.com injury report for the week, scraped in Actions and committed to data/model/official_injuries.json.
method.starter_rule: Projected starter = the lowest-ranked listed player at that slot who is not Out or Doubtful on the official report. Questionable counts as available but at risk and is shown, never upgraded or downgraded.
method.no_report_clubs: Clubs with no published report this week (on bye, or the club has filed nothing) are labelled 'no report published'. Their ladders are published but no starter is marked unavailable, because the absence of a report is not evidence of health.
limits: Club depth charts are a club publication, not a league filing; several are labelled unofficial by the club itself and the label is carried through.
The chart is a weekly snapshot. Practice-squad elevations, trades and late scratches are not modelled.
Game status is a designation, not proof of who plays.
HOU publishes no depth chart; its rows are blank by design.

gates.name: walk-forward / pre-game information only
gates.why: Every input to the bet decision is known before kick-off and, for the model rules, comes from a fit that used only earlier games.

gates.name: observed prices on every scored bet
gates.why: Every scored bet carries a price taken from the source file. No -110 assumption is used.

gates.name: at least 200 scored bets
gates.why: Below this, a run of luck is indistinguishable from skill at any plausible effect size.

gates.name: hit rate beats the break-even implied by the actual prices taken
gates.why: Break-even is computed from the real price on each bet, not from 0.5.

gates.name: survives multiple testing (BH-adjusted p < 0.05, 12 rules tested)
gates.why: Testing many rules and reporting only the best one manufactures winners; the Benjamini-Hochberg step charges for that.

gates.name: positive in a untouched holdout (2024 + 2025)
gates.why: The holdout seasons were never used to tune the rule thresholds.

gates.name: positive in at least 60% of individual seasons
gates.why: An edge that exists in only one season is a season, not a strategy.

gates.name: 95% bootstrap confidence interval on ROI excludes zero
gates.why: Ten thousand resamples of the actual bet log; the interval must sit above zero.

model_gates.rule: Every input file pinned by URL and sha256.
Rule fixed before evaluation; no threshold search.
Positive ROI across the two most recent seasons.
Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.10 against break-even win rate.
At least 60% of tested seasons positive.
Max drawdown no worse than -25 units.

luck.method: Null: the observed prices are fair, so a 1-unit bet at decimal d has mean profit 0 and variance d-1. The standard deviation of total profit is then sqrt(sum(d_i - 1)) over the bets actually placed. No simulation and no assumption beyond independence of bets.
luck.note: The last column is the number of bets the strategy would need before an edge of the observed size could be detected 80% of the time at the 5% level. Where that number is larger than any realistic season, the honest answer is that the sample cannot settle the question.

signal.method: Signal = 100 x (win rate - 0.5), normal 95% interval, two-sided z test against a coin flip. The money column is the board's own ROI at the prices it used. Both are printed because they answer different questions. Benjamini-Hochberg q across every rule on both boards (24 tests). Two nulls are reported per rule because they answer different questions: H0 = a coin flip (is there a signal at all?) and H0 = the break-even rate implied by the price actually taken (does the signal survive the price?). The board's own published p is recomputed here from its n, wins and break-even rate; a cell that does not reproduce is flagged.
